title: Enriched Parquet Refs: Design & Integration
text: GDAL already reads kerchunk parquet via /vsikerchunk/. enriched format superset - extra columns ignored, (path, offset, length) positions. fully leverage enriched metadata, GDAL need : Read parquet file-level KV metadata .zarray/.zattrs (instead requiring sidecar JSON files) Apply tiff_predictor filter (earlier PR) Expose geotransform CRS parquet metadata ~3 changes vsikerchunk_parquet_ref.cpp: - metadata synthesis step, check parquet KV pairs first - Fall sidecar .zarray/.zattrs found - Pass geotransform/CRS zarr driver’s dataset beauty backward compatibility: files without KV metadata still work via sidecar JSON path. Files KV metadata skip sidecar reads (fewer HTTP requests remote stores).

title: Enriched Parquet Refs: Design & Integration
text: zarr conflates storage layout codec specification. virtualise TIFF tiles zarr chunks, inherit zarr’s assumption codec chain self-describing within zarr spec. TIFF predictor isn’t zarr codec. JPEG quantization tables aren’t zarr metadata. format-specific transform lives gap “bytes” “decode .” enriched parquet separates concerns: - Columns answer “bytes” (path, offset, length) - Spatial columns answer “bytes need” (bbox, time) - File metadata answers “decode ” (zarray full filter chain including format-specific transforms) zarr JSON embedded metadata, used store format. means codec spec can include non-standard filters (tiff_predictor) without breaking zarr implementation - parquet isn’t claiming zarr store. CAN consumed zarr (via /vsikerchunk/ zaro’s ReferenceStore), doesn’t .

title: Getting started
text: zaro_read() takes 0-based start count Zarr dimension order (TIME, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE); NA means rest axis.
code: gsla <- zaro_read(store, "GSLA", start = c(0, 0, 0), count = c(1, NA, NA),                   meta = ds$arrays$GSLA) dim(gsla) #>      TIME  LATITUDE LONGITUDE  #>         1       351       641 lon <- zaro_read(store, "LONGITUDE", meta = ds$arrays$LONGITUDE) lat <- zaro_read(store, "LATITUDE", meta = ds$arrays$LATITUDE) z <- t(gsla[1, , ]) image(as.vector(lon), as.vector(lat), z, asp = 1, zlim = c(-1, 1) * max(abs(z), na.rm = TRUE),       col = hcl.colors(64, "Blue-Red 3"), xlab = "longitude", ylab = "latitude",       main = "Gridded sea level anomaly (m), first time step")

text: sharded array, stored object (shard) packs many inner chunks, index one . zaro plans shard one level byte references: reads shard’s index one small ranged request, inner chunk byte range shard. Copernicus EOPF Sentinel-2 L2A product published sharded GeoZarr: 10 m band one 10980 x 10980 shard 45 x 45 inner chunks. zaro’s sharded reads checked zarr-python GDAL store, GDAL’s sharding test fixtures, arrays written zarr-python.

title: Virtual stores
text: lazy array cf = TRUE unpacks values masks fill. made-30-day track eastern Tasmania, diving 5 200 m: one value per day, 30 different chunks 30 different NetCDF files. 30 byte ranges fetched concurrently one connection pool. ’s default, 8 connections per host (options(zaro.max_con)).
code: temp <- zaro_array(ds, "temp", cf = TRUE)     # xt_ocean, yt_ocean, st_ocean, Time dim(temp) #> [1] 3600 1500   51 5479  coord <- function(nm) as.vector(zaro_read(bran, nm, meta = ds$arrays[[nm]])) xt <- coord("xt_ocean"); yt <- coord("yt_ocean"); st <- coord("st_ocean") units <- ds$arrays$Time@attributes$units; units #> [1] "days since 1979-01-01" ## time steps are at midday (x.5 days): floor them to their calendar day time <- as.Date(sub("^days since ", "", units)) + floor(coord("Time"))  track <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2023-03-01") + 0:29,                     lon = seq(147.8, 152.5, length.out = 30),                     lat = seq(-43.5, -39.0, length.out = 30),                     depth = round(5 + 195 * (1 - cos(seq(0, pi, length.out = 30))) / 2)) near <- function(coord, v) vapply(v, function(z) which.min(abs(coord - z)), 1L) idx <- cbind(near(xt, track$lon), near(yt, track$lat), near(st, track$depth),              near(as.numeric(time), as.numeric(track$date)))  system.time(track$temp <- temp[idx]) #>    user  system elapsed  #>   0.539   0.128   1.024 head(track) #>         date      lon       lat depth     temp #> 1 2023-03-01 147.8000 -43.50000     5 16.85644 #> 2 2023-03-02 147.9621 -43.34483     6 17.08991 #> 3 2023-03-03 148.1241 -43.18966     7 17.78253 #> 4 2023-03-04 148.2862 -43.03448    10 18.36619 #> 5 2023-03-05 148.4483 -42.87931    14 18.66192 #> 6 2023-03-06 148.6103 -42.72414    19 18.92651 plot(track$date, track$temp, type = "b", pch = 19, xlab = "", ylab = "temperature (degC)",      main = "BRAN2023 along a made-up track")

title: Zarr via Arrow
text: Three internal layers, one flat API. Store - key-value access Zarr stores. Arrow FileSystem handles local, S3, GCS natively. gdalraster VSI handles HTTP provides automatic S3 region detection Arrow returns 301 redirect. Kerchunk JSON Parquet reference stores provide virtual Zarr access existing archival files (NetCDF, HDF5, GRIB, TIFF). Metadata - pure R/jsonlite parsing automatic V2/V3 detection. Consolidated metadata preferred cloud stores: .zmetadata (V2) consolidated zarr.json (V3), retrieving array metadata single request. Handles numpy dtype strings, xarray’s _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS convention, JSON-encoded fill values ("NaN", "Infinity"). Codec - decompression pipeline using Arrow C++ codecs (zstd, gzip, lz4, brotli, snappy, bz2) optional blosc fallback V2 stores. V2 compressor + filters normalised V3 codec chain model decode pipeline uniform. Type coercion handles endianness dtype mapping R vectors via readBin().

title: Zarr via Arrow
text: core functions:
code: store <- zaro(source, ...)       # open a store zaro_list(store)                 # list contents zaro_meta(store, path)           # read metadata zaro_read(store, path, ...)      # read array data zaro_dataset(store)              # every array and its dimensions, no data read zaro_array(store, path, cf = TRUE)  # a lazy R array (via altarr), CF-decoded

title: Zarr via Arrow
text: Version detection automatic. zaro_meta() tries V3 first (zarr.json), falls back V2 (.zmetadata consolidated, per-array .zarray + .zattrs). Essentially existing cloud Zarr data (AODN, Copernicus, CMIP6, NASA) V2 - fully supported. V2 specifics handled: numpy dtype strings (<f4, >i2, |u1), dimension_separator (dot slash), _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS (xarray), C/F memory order, consolidated .zmetadata, fill value coercion JSON strings.

title: Zarr via Arrow
text: zarr (CRAN) - native R Zarr V3 implementation R6 store/codec architecture. zaro contribute Arrow-backed store class. Different approach: zarr aims spec-complete V3, zaro prioritises cloud access existing V2 data. pizzarr - pure R Zarr V2 implementation HTTP store support. Bioimaging origin. gdalraster - comprehensive GDAL bindings including Zarr driver Multidimensional API. backend ndr. zaro GDAL-independent array semantics codec pipeline, uses GDAL VSI filesystem access Arrow doesn’t cover transport (HTTP, cross-region S3). tidync - metadata-first NetCDF exploration. zaro sits potential backend infrastructure Zarr sources. ndr - S7-based xarray-like labeled arrays R. gdalraster Multidim backend primary driver. zaro alternative backend GDAL-independent Zarr access direct store-level control. vapour - lightweight GDAL bindings raster vector data. Provides VSI filesystem access zaro uses via gdalraster. altarr (hypertidy/altarr) – lazy chunked arrays plain R arrays (ALTREP). zaro_array() uses zaro’s chunk fetch codec pipeline altarr fetch function, Zarr array subsets reduces base R, reading chunks needs.

title: Zarr via Arrow
text: zaro implements Zarr specification directly rather wrapping Zarr library. Capabilities interoperate Python ecosystem shared specifications: JSON metadata, codec algorithms (via Arrow’s C++ implementations, identical PyArrow), S3 protocols, chunk layout. dataset written xarray Python reads zaro without conversion.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: Initial version.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: Arrow-backed Zarr reader R. Implements Zarr specification directly using Arrow C++ filesystem access, compression codecs, byte buffers. dependency zarr-python Zarr-specific C/Rust library. S7 class ZaroMeta parsed array group metadata, uniform representation across Zarr V2 V3. Store abstraction layer ArrowStore (local, S3, GCS via Arrow FileSystem), VSIStore (HTTP fallback S3 via gdalraster), ReferenceStore (Kerchunk JSON references), VirtualiZarrStore (Parquet manifest reference stores). Designed future backends (Icechunk) without changing read pipeline. Codec pipeline normalised across V2 V3. V2’s single compressor plus filters list mapped V3-style codec chains decode path uniform.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: Parse .zarray, .zgroup, .zattrs metadata. Consolidated metadata via .zmetadata - single HTTP request retrieves metadata arrays V2 store. Numpy dtype string parsing (<f4, >i2, |u1, etc.) endianness detection. _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS convention dimension names (xarray compatibility). dimension_separator handling (dot-separated slash-separated chunk keys). fill_value coercion JSON strings ("NaN", "Infinity") R numeric values. sanitize_json() handles Python-flavoured JSON bare NaN, Infinity, -Infinity values invalid strict JSON.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: Parse zarr.json metadata including codecs, dimension names, fill values, chunk grid configuration. Consolidated V3 metadata (single zarr.json embedded node metadata).

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: New VirtualiZarrStore backend directory-layout Parquet reference stores produced VirtualiZarr. provide Zarr-style access existing archival files (NetCDF, HDF5, GRIB) without reformatting. Metadata layer (.zmetadata) fetched via curl - GDAL-free. Chunk manifests (refs.N.parq shards) loaded via arrow::read_parquet() lazy per-variable loading environment-based caching. C-order linearization maps chunk grid indices manifest row positions stores without explicit chunk key columns. Inline data support via raw column manifests (used coordinate variables whose data stored directly Parquet rather byte-range references). Byte-range reads source files via byte_range_read() supporting Arrow S3/GCS, gdalraster VSI, curl HTTP - full chain GDAL-free using curl. URI scheme: virtualizarr://https://example.com/dataset.parq virtualizarr:///local/path/dataset.parq. Tested BRAN2023 ocean temperature (5479 time steps, 51 depth levels, 1500x3600 spatial grid, 104 manifest shards, NCI THREDDS byte-range serving).

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: S3 stores via Arrow S3FileSystem automatic fallback gdalraster /vsis3/ 301 region redirects. Anonymous access propagation (anonymous = TRUE maps AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST Arrow GDAL backends). GCS stores via Arrow GcsFileSystem. HTTP/HTTPS stores via gdalraster /vsicurl/.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: Hyperslab reads start/count indexing (0-based, following Zarr convention). Chunk coverage computation assembly across chunk boundaries. Blosc (lz4, zstd, zlib, snappy), gzip, zstd decompression via Arrow codecs. Safety coercion output array type fill value otherwise produce character array.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: Verbose messaging throughout ([zaro] ...), default discoverability. Silence verbose = FALSE suppressMessages(). Reports store backend, metadata format detected, dtype/shape/chunks/codecs, dimension names, chunk counts reads.

title: zaro 0.0.1
text: AODN cloud-optimised Zarr stores (S3, ap-southeast-2, Zarr V2, blosc/lz4 compression, consolidated .zmetadata). BRAN2023 ocean temperature via VirtualiZarr Parquet references (NCI THREDDS byte-range reads, shuffle+zlib compression, int16 scale/offset packing).
